Flow: Tithe (10%). Stated purpose: Supporting the worldwide gospel work through the conference. How it controls: Medium — the flow is upward and away from local visibility, and it pays the salary of the pastor the congregation did not hire. Who benefits: The conference and union structures benefit..
Tithe (10%)

Flow: Local church budget offerings. Stated purpose: Running the congregation you actually attend. How it controls: Low — visible, local, and usually reported to the members. Who benefits: The local congregation benefits..
Local church budget offerings

Flow: Church school tuition. Stated purpose: Educating children in the faith. How it controls: Medium — a substantial recurring cost, and a strong retention mechanism as well as a genuine service. Who benefits: The education system benefits..
Church school tuition

Flow: Health system revenue. Stated purpose: Hospital and clinic operations. How it controls: Medium — large corporate entities whose executive pay is public in tax filings where the entity files but rarely surfaced to members. Who benefits: The health corporations and their executives benefit..
Health system revenue

Flow: Publishing and literature evangelism. Stated purpose: Spreading the message and employing colporteurs (literature evangelists). How it controls: Medium — a sales workforce paid on commission, historically with weak labour protections. Who benefits: The publishing houses benefit..
Publishing and literature evangelism

Flow: ADRA and disaster offerings. Stated purpose: Relief and development. How it controls: Low — independently evaluated in many jurisdictions and among the more checkable flows in this codex. Who benefits: The people it serves benefit, substantially and verifiably..
